references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the barren woman who will rejoice: 'Break forth and shout, you who are not in labor!' ([ref:Jes 54:1|Isaiah 54:1]). Jesus reverses this image, saying that in the coming days the barren will be considered blessed because they will escape seeing their children suffer during Jerusalem's destruction.

Hosea asks God to give them 'barren wombs and dried-up breasts' ([ref:Hos 9:14|Hosea 9:14]) as a form of mercy within judgment—it is better not to have children than to watch them be killed. Jesus uses similar reasoning regarding Jerusalem's coming destruction.

In Jesus' eschatological discourse, he says: 'Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!' ([ref:Luk 21:23|Luke 21:23]). This expresses the same idea—that mothers will suffer especially during times of distress, making childlessness a blessing.

In Matthew's version of the eschatological discourse, Jesus says: 'Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!' ([ref:Matt 24:19|Matthew 24:19]). Parallel to Luke 21:23, this shows that having children during the time of destruction will be an extra burden.

The context in [ref:Luk 23:28|Luke 23:28] is Jesus' words to the daughters of Jerusalem, telling them not to weep for him but for themselves and their children—this provides the direct background for the blessing pronounced on the barren in verse 29.

In [ref:Åp 6:16|Revelation 6:16], people cry out to the mountains: 'Fall on us and hide us!'—which directly follows the thought from Luke 23:30 and shows that the judgment Jesus warns of in verse 29 has eschatological scope.

Elizabeth says that the Lord has taken away her disgrace among people ([ref:Luk 1:25|Luke 1:25]). Childlessness was regarded as a shame in Israel, but Jesus completely reverses this in his prophecy about Jerusalem's fall—the childless will be called blessed.

Rachel says to Jacob: 'Give me children, or I shall die!' ([ref:1 Mos 30:1|Genesis 30:1]). In the Old Testament, childlessness was a deep sorrow and disgrace, but Jesus prophesies that this understanding will be turned upside down in the time of judgment.
